Yelp New Orleans Restaurant Analysis

A portfolio project in data cleaning, joins, spatial analysis, and reviewer-adjusted ratings

Author

Brandon Lee

Research question

Portfolio README · AI assistance log · Report source

Where can someone find the top 15 restaurants for New Orleans cooking—Cajun/Creole, Seafood, Southern, or Soul Food—in New Orleans, and which geographic area is best for finding them?

Executive summary

The initial New Orleans cooking filter contains 672 restaurants and 250,304 reviews. The official Census city check retains 656 restaurants and 249,002 reviews for the geographic analysis. Both ZCTAs and wards contain restaurants in 17 areas; wards are selected for the main comparison because their restaurant counts are more balanced and fewer areas have very small samples. Two lakefront restaurants remain unmatched to wards. Final restaurant eligibility, reviewer-adjusted scores, the top 15, and a final best-area conclusion remain outstanding.

Data and large-file handling

The import scans the complete Yelp business and review JSON files in pages, filters New Orleans restaurants, and retains only the review columns needed for ratings analysis. It saves compressed RDS files so subsequent analysis does not reload the raw JSON. Filtered reviews are accumulated in memory; this is not a fully disk-backed workflow. Review text and voting fields are omitted. The selected review records span March 14, 2005 through January 19, 2022. The user reported that RStudio became unresponsive while working with the large data. Loading and verifying the smaller filtered RDS files in a separate R process avoided depending on that frozen session; no memory measurements were collected, so the cause of the freeze is unknown.

Run Rscript R/analysis.R from the repository root to reproduce the descriptive tables and figures using the saved theme RDS files. This script uses ggplot2. See the restaurant summary, missing-value audit, restaurants with blank addresses, and validation checks.

Restaurant definition and cleaning

Filter to Yelp city New Orleans, state LA, and exact category token Restaurants. Keep both open and closed businesses for the initial historical subset, retain coordinates for later spatial joins, and convert empty postal codes to missing values. See the cleaning code and import code.

Category selection

Selected theme: New Orleans cooking. Include restaurants matching at least one of Cajun/Creole, Seafood, Southern, or Soul Food; count each business once. The planned final ranking contains 15 restaurants. See category selection for counts and co-occurrence evidence.

Initial descriptive results

The filtered theme contains 672 restaurants and 250,304 reviews from 138,848 distinct reviewers. Reviews span 2005-03-14 to 2022-01-19.

Data quality

The missing-value audit found 0 NA values and 7 blank text fields. Details are shown below.

Duplicate-ID, review-linkage, rating-range, coordinate-range, date-parsing, and open-status checks found no issues. Range checks do not establish coordinate accuracy, and absence of missing values does not establish overall accuracy.

restaurants address 0 7

The seven blank street addresses are retained because coordinates are present. They have not been imputed or independently checked; see the exported missing-address table for follow-up.

435 businesses are marked open and 237 marked closed in the historical snapshot. No open-status exclusion has been applied; these flags do not verify current operating status.

What remains

Steps 3–6: categories, joins, and geography

Step 3: category evidence

The selected New Orleans cooking theme connects Cajun/Creole, seafood, Southern, and soul-food traditions. A restaurant qualifies by matching at least one selected category, rather than all four. The labels are an operational definition, not proof that every menu is uniquely local. Category memberships overlap.

The initial city-label subset contains 672 restaurants. After the explicit city-boundary check below, 656 restaurants remain in the geographic comparison:

The selected group occupies 17 ZCTAs and all 17 wards. Both systems exceed the requirement of 10 restaurants across seven geographic areas. Category-by-area counts, average ratings, and review volumes are exported in category_by_area.csv.

Step 4: businesses joined to reviews

Reviews were filtered before joining. An explicit many-to-one join on business_id attaches business names and categories to every selected review, preserving review IDs and the row count. The joined review-level RDS is saved locally as data/new_orleans/reviews_cooking_joined.rds; the smaller audit is committed.

The later city-only geographic subset contains 249,002 reviews for 656 restaurants. The original 250,304-review subset is preserved; the new city-only RDS files are separate.

Step 5: official city-boundary check

All 2,259 initial New Orleans restaurant locations were spatially joined to 2020 Census Louisiana place polygons using sf::st_join and st_within. The join assigns 2,202 to New Orleans and 57 to other Census places; no locations lack a place match. Among the selected theme, 656 are in New Orleans and 16 are assigned to nearby places such as Jefferson, Harahan, and Elmwood.

For the main geographic comparison, use the official city-contained subset so ZCTAs and wards describe the same city. This is an explicit analytical scope choice, not deletion of the original records. City-label mismatches may reflect postal labeling, geocoding, mobile businesses, or boundary differences; their specific causes are not established. The export includes place names and distances to the city for review. Le Petit Bistro, for example, has a blank address and coordinates in Kenner despite a New Orleans postal label and requires further checking.

All place assignments · Selected restaurants outside the city

Step 6: ZCTAs compared with wards

Restaurant coordinates are transformed from longitude/latitude (EPSG:4326) to NAD83 / Louisiana South in metres (EPSG:26982). Polygon validity is repaired before spatial joins. The same 656 city-contained locations are joined to each system with st_within. No nearest-area assignment or snapping is applied. The joins are checked for duplicated businesses and boundary-touching points.

System Populated areas Assigned Unmatched Min count* Max count
ZCTA 17 656 0 2 213
Ward 17 654 2 5 116

*Minimum among populated areas. Of 35 ZCTA polygons intersecting the city, 18 contain no selected city restaurants and five populated ZCTAs contain fewer than 10. All 17 wards contain selected restaurants, and only Ward 16 has fewer than 10 (five). Empty and small areas are retained in the exported summaries. Empty areas have no rating, not a rating of zero.

The two unmatched ward locations are Felix’s Restaurant & Oyster Bar and Brisbi’s Lakefront Restaurant & Bar, both at 7400 Lakeshore Drive. They fall inside the Census city but approximately 16.3 and 13.4 metres outside the nearest Ward 4 polygon. These shoreline discrepancies could reflect coordinate or boundary precision; they are not corrected without further evidence. Both receive ZCTA 70124. They remain in the city dataset and are omitted only from ward-level aggregates.

Complete comparison · Unmatched ward locations

The full-city maps preserve the geographic context; the urban-detail panels make the dense restaurant cluster readable. Colors describe counts in the full source areas, using only city-contained restaurants. Displayed boundaries are clipped to the Census city. ZCTAs are Census approximations of postal service areas, not neighborhoods; wards are the City’s numbered divisions, not neighborhood labels.

Main geographic choice: wards

Use wards for the main area comparison and keep ZCTAs as the sensitivity comparison. Wards divide this restaurant pool more evenly: the median populated-area count is 25 versus 16 for ZCTAs, the largest ward contains 116 restaurants versus 213 in the largest ZCTA, and only one ward has fewer than 10 restaurants versus five populated ZCTAs. Both systems offer 17 populated areas. Wards therefore reduce the number of very small samples while retaining city-specific numbered areas that can be shown clearly on maps. This choice follows coverage and sample-size evidence, not which system yields a higher rating.

The tradeoffs are the two unmatched lakefront points, the need to explain ward numbers to visitors, and broad wards that can hide variation within an area. Ward 16’s five restaurants are too few for a strong area-level recommendation; its rating remains descriptive. ZCTAs offer familiar postal-style identifiers and complete assignment of the city subset, so both sets of results remain available. Restaurant counts measure selection, not density per square kilometre or travel convenience.

Ward 4 has the most qualifying restaurants (116); Ward 13 has the highest mean business rating among wards with at least 10 restaurants (4.15, n=20), narrowly ahead of Ward 8 (4.147, n=17). This is not enough to declare a final best area. ZCTA 70130 has the largest selection (213), while 70117 leads populated ZCTAs with at least 10 restaurants in raw mean stars (4.13, n=30). Ratings must still be checked against reviewer adjustment and final eligibility rules.

Boundary sources and time limitations

Census boundaries: 2020 TIGER/Line place files and 2020 cartographic ZCTA boundaries, obtained with tigris. Wards: City of New Orleans Enterprise GIS, Administrative Layers, Wards layer 3, downloaded October 29, 2026. The ward service does not state a historical effective date; it is a saved current-service snapshot, not verified 2020 ward geometry. Yelp reviews span 2005–2022, so neither boundary set proves which area applied at every review date. Saved boundaries, source metadata, and checksums support reproduction; no demographic or causal claims are made.

Ratings and reviewer adjustment

Step 7 remains outstanding. Use the city-only RDS files for the next stage, calculate reviewer baselines and adjusted scores, compare all reviewers with eligible reviewers, justify restaurant and reviewer activity thresholds, and test ranking sensitivity. Then produce the final top 15 table and ward-boundary map. The current raw area means are descriptive, not the final ranking.

Conclusions and limitations

Steps 3–6 are complete: the category evidence and review join are documented, city-label mismatches are audited, and ZCTAs and wards are compared with counts, raw ratings, and maps. Wards offer the more balanced restaurant pool for the main comparison. Category overlap, small samples, historical boundary differences, two unmatched lakefront points, and the 2005–2022 review window limit interpretation. The final top 15 and best area require Step 7 and the final synthesis.

Completion audit
